title: Formulary Benefit Exception Approval Terms: Length, Renewal, Strength and Out-of-Pocket
content:
For each formulary of the Formulary Benefit, this table gives the standard approval length in months, the expedited approval length in days, the renewal lead time, whether an approval carries over to other strengths, and whether cost share paid under an approval counts toward the out-of-pocket maximum.

| Term | Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard approval length (calendar months) | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| Expedited approval length (calendar days, the exigency period) | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Renewal accepted from this many calendar days before expiration | 30 | 30 | 45 | 45 | 60 | 60 |
| Approval also covers other strengths of the same drug | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Cost share paid under an approval counts toward the out-of-pocket maximum | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

## How the figures read

- The standard approval length is a number of calendar months counted from the approval effective date. Where the closing day-of-month does not exist, the month-end fallback applies.
- The renewal lead is counted back from the current approval's expiration date. A renewal is a new request.
- Where the strength column reads *no*, an approval covers only the drug and strength requested.

*Hypothetical renewal window.* Take an approval expiring on 30 June. On the Northbridge Broad Formulary (60 days) a renewal request is accepted from 1 May. On the Northbridge Value Formulary (30 days) it is accepted from 31 May.
